But it's also hard for someone like me who shops at more than one store to use this app to see if I can save money. I'd love to see the ability to use more than one store in a week's plan, as well as include things I need to buy anyway for breakfast or beverages, etc in the grocery bill line. title: Great concept but...
body: There are a lot of things I like about this app! I came to this app from Mealime (RIP 🙏 (IYKYK)) and it has a lot of similar features that are cool (like building a shopping list based on my meal plan) and even some things that are better (e.g. being able to add things to my kitchen/pantry so they don't show up in my list every week)! That said, I do take issue with some of the recipes. So far I've made 3-4 recipes from TapCook and idk if they're written by AI or what but the steps often do not make sense; it feels to me like steps are often missing, out of order, or incompatible with each other. The food tastes good but the process is tough and sometimes leads to mistakes that could be avoided if the instructions were clearer. So I guess I would say: this app is good if you know enough about cooking to identify errors/inconsistencies in the recipes and adjust accordingly but if you are new to cooking maybe give it a pass and find something with better directions.

title: Meh
body: I didn’t get very far with it. It makes you think it’s really customizable, but then it’s not. Yes, you can check off a bunch of pantry staples, and exclude some allergens, and things you won’t eat. But you can’t add ANYTHING that you specifically want to have. For example, I don’t eat white rice, but I love brown rice. Not on the list. I don’t buy broths, but I do use bouillons. Also not on the list. So while it’s a great idea in theory, one of the apps where you can actually add the items in your pantry and/or actually cook with, and then create recipes from them are probably more practical in the long run. I also did not find the prices to be very accurate. On the day I checked, the app had a 2lb bag of frozen shrimp (unspecified size) for $13.83. My Walmart had various 2lb bags at $17.97, $15.96, and $16.62. So the grand total of what the app said I was going to spend on my weekly groceries was probably way off too.

I’ve tried so many ways to get into cooking more whole food meals while also being conscious of what we spend on groceries. This is the first time I’ve felt like I found a real solution! I can’t believe how easy this app is from start to finish. The recipes and meals we’ve had so far have been delicious and pretty easy and straightforward. I’m so excited to continue discovering new foods and cooking regularly! The yearly subscription cost is well worth it in my opinion.

title: Pleasantly surprised
body: I downloaded this app and subscribed to the free trial. Then I forgot about it and accidentally purchased the year subscription… I AM SO GLAD THAT HAPPENED!! I figured I might as well give it an honest try since I’ve paid for the year and it’s seriously been a godsend. I’m a full time working mom of three, my husband is in school, I’m starting grad school soon, and I was spending hours a week meal planning, making grocery lists, grocery shopping and stressing the whole time about staying under budget. With this app I can do it all in minutes, the meals are all super good and easy to make. My kids, all 6 and under, have enjoyed every single meal and they’re being exposed to types of food we haven’t eaten much of before. I feel like I’ve been hunting my whole adult life for recipes like these. I’ve already told everyone that will hear me about the app. It’s one thing to take off the mental load of having to meal plan but it also saves me money, saves me time, and is yummy and nutritious. If I could give it 10 stars I would.

title: Almost perfect
body: The only complaint I have at this point is that the recipes don’t have any preparation steps for the ingredients. For example it just says, “fry bok choy stems then leaves.” How should the bok choy be cut? Sliced in half, chopped? I had to reference the picture to find out. Also, it asks for salt, but never reminds you to add it during the cooking steps. Now, I know how to cook, but I imagine some newbie forgetting and getting bland steak. I think the devs could easily add the preparation steps, or at least descriptions of the desired form in the line for each ingredient. I assume these are mostly AI recipes anyway, so it shouldn’t be that hard.

title: Needs more personalization
body: App is a great concept but needs more preferences. The “won’t eat” section is very limited right now. For people with 0 picky eaters in the family, the app is great. However, for those who have picky eaters and/or those allergic to certain foods, it needs some work. Won’t eat section should include a lot more things like won’t eat “dark meat, pork, peanuts, shell fish (or other allergy related foods). Also maybe include a healthy section like only lean meats, low fat diets etc. I get it, the app is new and designed to save money at the store. But again it doesn’t work too well for picky eaters and allergic people. (I myself am not a picky eater and I can’t control what a kid likes/doesn’t like or what people are allergic to).
